name: Self-discipline
blurb: Acting on what you decided when you no longer feel like it, without relying on willpower alone.

levels.beginner: Stop treating discipline as a character trait. Pick one small commitment, make it absurdly easy to start, and reduce the friction and temptation around it before you rely on resolve.
levels.intermediate: You can hold a streak but collapse under stress or disruption. Build recovery rules for missed days, and separate the systems that need discipline from the ones that should be automated or eliminated.
levels.advanced: Discipline stops being the bottleneck and identity does. Design commitments you would keep under bad conditions, and audit which of your rules still serve a goal you actually hold.

name: Beating procrastination
blurb: Understanding why you avoid specific tasks and reducing the emotional cost of starting them.

levels.beginner: Notice that procrastination is mood repair, not laziness. Name the feeling the task triggers, then shrink the first step until it is too small to trigger it.
levels.intermediate: Tackle the structural causes: unclear next actions, tasks that hide a decision you haven't made, and deadlines too distant to feel real. Break work down until each item names a physical action.
levels.advanced: Address chronic avoidance patterns tied to self-worth or fear of evaluation, and recognise when persistent avoidance is signalling a genuine mismatch between you and the work.

name: Anxiety management
blurb: Learning practical, evidence-supported ways to reduce anxiety's grip without avoiding your life.

levels.beginner: Learn what anxiety physically is and why avoidance strengthens it. Start with basic grounding and breathing tools and a habit of naming what you are actually worried about.
levels.intermediate: Work with exposure rather than reassurance: face avoided situations gradually and deliberately, and learn to spot the safety behaviours that keep the fear alive.
levels.advanced: Address the deeper maintaining patterns — intolerance of uncertainty, rumination, and chronic hypervigilance — and know when a self-help approach should become professional treatment.

name: Confidence building
blurb: Building justified self-trust through evidence and competence rather than affirmation.

levels.beginner: Separate confidence from self-esteem and from arrogance. Start collecting evidence you can actually do things by taking small actions you have been avoiding.
levels.intermediate: Work on the gap between competence and felt confidence: how you interpret failure, how you talk to yourself, and how much you calibrate your worth to other people's reactions.
levels.advanced: Develop confidence that survives genuine failure and public criticism, and learn to hold accurate self-assessment without either inflation or collapse.

name: Emotional regulation
blurb: Feeling strong emotions without being run by them, and recovering faster when you are.

levels.beginner: Learn to label emotions accurately and notice their physical signature early, before the point where you can no longer choose your response.
levels.intermediate: Build a repertoire of regulation strategies and learn which fits which situation — reappraisal, distraction, acceptance, and changing the situation itself all have different costs.
levels.advanced: Work on the patterns beneath repeated reactions: what the emotion is protecting, and how to stay regulated in relationships and conflicts where the stakes are highest.

name: Cognitive biases
blurb: Recognising the predictable ways your own reasoning goes wrong, and building habits that partly correct for them.

levels.beginner: Learn the major, well-replicated biases and where they show up in ordinary decisions. Knowing the names is a starting point, not a fix.
levels.intermediate: Move from recognising biases in hindsight to building decision procedures — base rates, outside view, pre-mortems, and written predictions — that reduce them in advance.
levels.advanced: Understand the live methodological debates about which effects replicate, calibrate your own forecasts against outcomes, and notice the bias of thinking bias-awareness makes you immune.

name: Habit formation
blurb: Making a behaviour automatic enough that it no longer needs a decision each day.

levels.beginner: Attach a very small behaviour to an existing cue and repeat it in a stable context. Consistency of context matters more than size or intensity at this stage.
levels.intermediate: Design for disruption: travel, illness, and schedule changes are what actually break habits. Work on breaking unwanted habits by changing cues and increasing friction.
levels.advanced: Understand what the research does and does not support about automaticity and timelines, and build habit systems that survive major life changes rather than ideal weeks.

name: Resilience after setbacks
blurb: Recovering function and perspective after failure, rejection, or loss without pretending it didn't hurt.

levels.beginner: Learn the difference between resilience and suppression. Restore the basics first — sleep, movement, contact with people — before trying to reframe anything.
levels.intermediate: Work on the explanatory habits that extend a setback: treating a specific failure as permanent, pervasive, and personal. Practise extracting the usable lesson without self-attack.
levels.advanced: Build the capacity to take repeated, meaningful risks over years, and to distinguish resilience worth having from stubbornly enduring a situation you should leave.

name: Burnout recovery
blurb: Recognising burnout as a condition of your situation, not a personal failing, and changing what caused it.

levels.beginner: Learn to recognise burnout's actual components — exhaustion, cynicism, reduced efficacy — and stop treating rest as something you earn after the work is finished.
levels.intermediate: Address the drivers rather than the symptoms: workload, autonomy, fairness, and value mismatch. A holiday does not fix a job that reliably produces burnout.
levels.advanced: Rebuild a sustainable relationship with ambitious work, including the harder structural decisions about role, boundaries, or leaving, and how to protect recovery once it starts.

name: Self-awareness
blurb: Seeing your own patterns, motives, and effect on others more accurately than introspection alone allows.

levels.beginner: Start with structured reflection — regular journalling with specific prompts — and learn why asking yourself 'why' often produces confident, wrong answers.
levels.intermediate: Seek external data: solicited feedback, recorded behaviour, and the discrepancy between your intentions and your reported effect on other people.
levels.advanced: Work on the deeper material — recurring relational patterns, defences, and the stories you use to explain yourself — usually with help rather than alone.

name: Overcoming perfectionism
blurb: Lowering the cost of imperfect work so you can ship, learn, and stop tying output to self-worth.

levels.beginner: Distinguish high standards from perfectionism: one is about the work, the other about what the work says about you. Practise deliberately finishing something at 80 percent.
levels.intermediate: Work on the specific mechanisms — over-checking, over-preparing, avoiding evaluation — and set explicit 'good enough' criteria before starting a piece of work.
levels.advanced: Address the self-worth contingency underneath, and build the ability to publish, be criticised, and keep going without either collapse or defensiveness.

name: Understanding therapy
blurb: Knowing what the main therapeutic approaches actually do, so you can choose and use treatment well.

levels.beginner: Learn what the major modalities are for and what a first session involves, plus how to find and vet a therapist and what therapy is not.
levels.intermediate: Understand how to be an active participant: setting goals, doing between-session work, raising ruptures, and recognising when an approach isn't fitting you.
levels.advanced: Engage with the evidence base and its limits — what modalities have support for which conditions, common factors, and the debates about outcome measurement.

name: Grief and loss
blurb: Living with bereavement and major loss without forcing it into stages or a timeline.

levels.beginner: Learn what grief actually looks like, why the stage model is not how it works, and what practical support in the first weeks and months looks like.
levels.intermediate: Work with the oscillation between loss and restoration, handle secondary losses and anniversaries, and rebuild routine without treating that as disloyalty.
levels.advanced: Understand prolonged and complicated grief, grief that follows ambiguous or stigmatised losses, and how to support others through it without platitudes.

name: Decision making
blurb: Making choices under uncertainty deliberately — weighing options, deciding when to decide, and judging the decision separately from the outcome.

levels.beginner: Learn to separate a decision from its outcome — a good call can lose and a bad one can win. Start writing down what you expected before you find out.
levels.intermediate: Work with explicit alternatives and stated assumptions, notice which decisions are reversible and can be made fast, and calibrate how confident you actually are.
levels.advanced: Handle decisions with genuinely conflicting values or long feedback loops, decide well as a group without averaging everyone into mush, and review past calls honestly enough to learn from them.

name: Journaling
blurb: Writing regularly about your own life in a way that produces something — clarity, a record, a decision — rather than just filling pages.

levels.beginner: Start small and unstructured enough that you actually do it. The habit matters more than the method, and most people quit because they set the bar at an essay.
levels.intermediate: Use prompts or formats that suit what you want out of it — processing an emotion, thinking a problem through, and keeping a record are different jobs needing different approaches.
levels.advanced: Reread deliberately rather than only writing, use the archive to notice patterns you would otherwise forget, and recognise when journaling has become rumination rather than reflection.

name: Strength training
blurb: Getting genuinely stronger with barbell and dumbbell work under a structured, progressive program.

levels.beginner: Learn a handful of compound lifts with acceptable technique and run a simple linear progression. Almost any well-structured program works if you actually run it.
levels.intermediate: Linear progression stops. Move to periodised programming with planned variation in intensity and volume, and learn to autoregulate around fatigue and life stress.
levels.advanced: Manage long training blocks, weak-point analysis, and technique refinement at loads where small errors matter, with realistic expectations about rate of progress.

name: Calisthenics
blurb: Building strength and skill with bodyweight movement, from first pull-up to advanced holds.

levels.beginner: Build the base: push-ups, rows, squats, and assisted pull-up progressions, with enough volume and consistency to make the first unassisted reps happen.
levels.intermediate: Progress through structured skill work — dips, weighted pull-ups, pistol squats, handstand — and add load rather than only chasing higher rep counts.
levels.advanced: Train the high-tension static skills (planche, front lever, one-arm work) with the long timelines and joint preparation they genuinely require.

name: Muscle building
blurb: Training and programming specifically to add muscle size, using what the evidence actually supports.

levels.beginner: Understand that muscle growth needs sufficient volume, proximity to failure, progression, and enough food and protein. Start with a simple full-body or upper-lower split.
levels.intermediate: Learn volume landmarks per muscle group, exercise selection for weak points, and how to structure mesocycles with deloads instead of grinding indefinitely.
levels.advanced: Refine technique for stimulus rather than load, manage fatigue across long blocks, and hold realistic expectations about rates of gain and the limits of the research.

name: Powerlifting
blurb: Maximising squat, bench, and deadlift for competition, with technique and peaking as the core skills.

levels.beginner: Learn the three competition lifts to the rulebook standard and run a novice program while building comfort with heavier singles.
levels.intermediate: Program in blocks, use RPE or percentage-based autoregulation, and address individual weak points and leverages rather than copying a famous lifter's routine.
levels.advanced: Peak accurately for a meet, manage attempt selection and cutting weight, and train around the accumulated niggles that come with years under heavy loads.

name: Running
blurb: Building a running habit and then running faster or further without repeatedly getting injured.

levels.beginner: Build the aerobic base slowly with run-walk progressions. Most beginner injuries come from increasing volume faster than tissue adapts.
levels.intermediate: Add structure: easy running as the bulk of volume, plus tempo and interval sessions, and learn to pace a race rather than run every run at the same effort.
levels.advanced: Periodise around goal races, work on running economy and strength support, and manage the trade-offs of high mileage against injury risk and life load.

name: Cycling
blurb: Riding better — position, pacing, and training — whether for fitness, commuting, or racing.

levels.beginner: Get a bike that fits, learn basic road skills and gearing, and build consistent easy riding volume before worrying about power numbers.
levels.intermediate: Train with structure using power or heart rate, learn to pace climbs and long rides, and fuel properly for rides over about ninety minutes.
levels.advanced: Periodise around events, work on race craft and group skills, and use testing and data analysis without letting the data replace the riding.

name: Swimming technique
blurb: Swimming with less effort and better position in the water rather than simply swimming harder.

levels.beginner: Get comfortable and horizontal in the water, learn to exhale underwater, and build a basic freestyle with a workable breathing pattern.
levels.intermediate: Refine body position, catch, and rotation with drills and video feedback, and start structuring sets rather than swimming continuous laps.
levels.advanced: Work on pacing, race-specific sets, open-water skills, and small technical refinements that only matter once the fundamentals are stable.

name: Mobility and flexibility
blurb: Increasing usable range of motion with strength through that range, not just passive stretching.

levels.beginner: Learn the difference between mobility and flexibility, and start a short consistent routine targeting the joints your daily life restricts most.
levels.intermediate: Add loaded and end-range strength work so new range is controllable, and target restrictions specific to your sport or training.
levels.advanced: Pursue demanding positions with realistic timelines, and understand what the evidence says about stretching's effects on performance and injury.

name: Yoga practice
blurb: Developing a sustainable yoga practice with sound alignment and a clear sense of what it is for.

levels.beginner: Learn the foundational postures and how to modify them for your body, and build a short regular practice rather than occasional long classes.
levels.intermediate: Develop breath-movement coordination, work on transitions and inversions with proper preparation, and choose styles deliberately for different purposes.
levels.advanced: Refine subtle alignment and build a self-directed practice, engaging with the tradition's philosophy while keeping claims about physical effects grounded.

name: Brazilian jiu-jitsu
blurb: Learning grappling systematically — positions, escapes, and submissions — through structured drilling and rolling.

levels.beginner: Focus on survival and escapes rather than submissions, learn the positional hierarchy, and get comfortable with the discomfort of being controlled.
levels.intermediate: Build a connected game with a few chosen positions and clear paths between them, and start pressure-testing against resisting partners of varied styles.
levels.advanced: Develop a personal system with counters to the counters, adapt training around injuries and age, and prepare specifically for competition rulesets.

name: Boxing and striking
blurb: Learning stance, footwork, and punching mechanics well enough that power comes from technique.

levels.beginner: Build stance, guard, and basic punches with correct weight transfer, plus footwork drilled slowly before speed or power.
levels.intermediate: Add combinations, defensive movement, and controlled sparring, learning to read distance and timing rather than only trading shots.
levels.advanced: Develop ring craft, tactical adaptation to opponent styles, and training that manages head-trauma risk seriously rather than treating hard sparring as toughness.

name: Rock climbing
blurb: Climbing better through movement skill and structured training, not just more sessions on the wall.

levels.beginner: Climb a lot, learn footwork and body positioning, and resist hangboarding early — technique and tendon readiness matter far more at this stage.
levels.intermediate: Add structured strength and finger training carefully, work on route reading and specific weaknesses, and learn to project rather than only flash.
levels.advanced: Periodise training around projects and seasons, manage finger and shoulder injury risk deliberately, and refine tactics for hard redpoints or highballs.

name: Injury prevention and rehab
blurb: Understanding load management and rehabilitation well enough to train around injury sensibly.

levels.beginner: Learn the basics of load management and why total rest is rarely the answer, plus when a symptom genuinely warrants professional assessment.
levels.intermediate: Understand progressive loading for tendon and muscle injuries, pain science fundamentals, and how to modify training rather than stopping entirely.
levels.advanced: Manage return-to-sport decisions, chronic or recurring issues, and the tension between what a scan shows and what the person actually reports.

name: Home workouts
blurb: Training effectively with minimal equipment and space, without pretending it's identical to a gym.

levels.beginner: Learn a small set of movements you can progress at home and build the consistency that a commute-free setup makes possible.
levels.intermediate: Apply real progressive overload with limited load — tempo, leverage, unilateral variations, and bands — and program rather than freestyle each session.
levels.advanced: Understand where home training genuinely plateaus for strength and size, and invest in the few equipment additions that remove those specific ceilings.

name: Sleep quality
blurb: Improving how well you actually sleep using behavioural methods with real evidence behind them.

levels.beginner: Fix the basics first: consistent wake time, light exposure, and a wind-down that doesn't depend on willpower. Track sleep loosely rather than obsessively.
levels.intermediate: Learn the components of CBT-I — stimulus control and sleep restriction — which have far stronger support than most sleep-hygiene advice.
levels.advanced: Understand circadian disorders, shift work, and the limits of consumer sleep tracking, and recognise when apnoea or another condition needs medical assessment.

name: Nutrition fundamentals
blurb: Building a diet that works from established basics rather than trends, and reading nutrition claims critically.

levels.beginner: Learn energy balance, protein, fibre, and food quality in plain terms, and build a few default meals rather than an elaborate plan you won't sustain.
levels.intermediate: Understand how to read a study versus a headline, adjust intake to goals and activity, and evaluate popular diets by their actual mechanisms.
levels.advanced: Engage with nutritional epidemiology's methodological limits, and understand where genuine scientific uncertainty sits versus where the evidence is settled.

name: Fat loss
blurb: Losing fat at a sustainable rate and, harder, keeping it off when the diet ends.

levels.beginner: Understand energy deficit and adherence, set a rate of loss you can actually maintain, and keep protein and resistance training in place to protect muscle.
levels.intermediate: Handle plateaus, adaptive changes in activity and hunger, diet breaks, and the behavioural side — eating out, social pressure, and tracking fatigue.
levels.advanced: Focus on maintenance as its own skill, understand weight regain research honestly, and know where medication and clinical support genuinely fit.

name: Sports nutrition
blurb: Eating to support training and recovery — timing, fuelling, and hydration for a specific sport.

levels.beginner: Get total intake and protein roughly right and stop under-fuelling training. Timing matters far less than adequacy at this stage.
levels.intermediate: Learn sport-specific carbohydrate and hydration strategies for training and competition, and practise race-day fuelling in training first.
levels.advanced: Periodise nutrition with training phases, understand relative energy deficiency and its consequences, and evaluate ergogenic aids by evidence quality.

name: Gut health
blurb: Separating what is actually known about digestion and the microbiome from a very noisy marketing space.

levels.beginner: Learn basic digestive function, the role of fibre and dietary variety, and why most symptoms do not need an elimination diet.
levels.intermediate: Understand structured approaches such as low-FODMAP as diagnostic tools with an endpoint, and how gut-brain interaction affects symptoms.
levels.advanced: Engage with the microbiome literature critically, understand what current testing can and cannot tell you, and recognise red-flag symptoms needing investigation.

name: Supplements literacy
blurb: Judging supplement claims by evidence and dose, and recognising that most of them do very little.

levels.beginner: Learn the short list with reasonable support, understand that supplements are lightly regulated, and check for third-party testing.
levels.intermediate: Read the actual evidence for a given compound — effect size, population, dose, and funding — rather than relying on a summary from a seller.
levels.advanced: Assess interactions, stacking claims, and the difference between a statistically significant result and a practically meaningful one.

name: Longevity and healthspan
blurb: Understanding what genuinely influences healthy lifespan, and how much of the field is still speculative.

levels.beginner: Start with the interventions that are well established — activity, sleep, smoking, alcohol, blood pressure — before anything exotic.
levels.intermediate: Understand cardiovascular and metabolic risk factors, screening, and how to interpret your own biomarkers without over-reacting to single readings.
levels.advanced: Engage critically with ageing biology, the gap between animal models and human outcomes, and the commercial incentives in longevity clinics and testing.

name: Posture and desk ergonomics
blurb: Setting up how you sit and work so long hours cost you less, without moralising about 'perfect posture'.

levels.beginner: Set up monitor height, chair, and input devices adequately, and build movement breaks in — position variety matters more than one ideal posture.
levels.intermediate: Address specific discomfort patterns with targeted strength and positioning changes, and adapt the setup for laptops, standing, and small spaces.
levels.advanced: Understand what the evidence actually shows about posture and pain, and treat persistent symptoms as a loading and health problem rather than a moral one.

name: Back pain management
blurb: Managing common back pain with movement and load rather than fear, and knowing the genuine warning signs.

levels.beginner: Learn that most back pain is non-specific and improves with movement, and that scans often show findings unrelated to symptoms.
levels.intermediate: Build graded activity and strength, work on pacing and flare-up management, and reduce the fear-avoidance that keeps pain persistent.
levels.advanced: Understand chronic pain mechanisms, when imaging or surgery is genuinely indicated, and how to keep training seriously with a history of back problems.

name: Addiction and recovery
blurb: Understanding dependence and the routes out of it, including drinking that never looks like rock bottom.

levels.beginner: Learn how dependence develops, honestly assess your own use, and understand that cutting down and stopping are different projects with different methods.
levels.intermediate: Work with triggers, cravings, and relapse as information rather than failure, and understand the main support routes including medication-assisted options.
levels.advanced: Address the underlying drivers, rebuild identity and social life without the substance, and support others without imposing one recovery model as the only valid one.

name: Skincare
blurb: Building a short, evidence-based routine and reading cosmetic marketing claims sceptically.

levels.beginner: Start with cleanser, moisturiser, and daily sunscreen. Most routines fail from too many actives too fast, not from missing an expensive product.
levels.intermediate: Learn the actives with real evidence — retinoids, and specific acids — and how to introduce them without wrecking your skin barrier.
levels.advanced: Understand formulation and concentration claims, treatment options for persistent conditions, and when a dermatologist beats another product.

name: Breathing techniques
blurb: Using deliberate breathing for calm, focus, or performance, with claims kept proportionate to evidence.

levels.beginner: Learn slow nasal breathing and a simple extended-exhale pattern, and use it in situations where you actually get anxious rather than only when calm.
levels.intermediate: Explore different protocols for different purposes, and understand the physiology of carbon dioxide tolerance and the vagal response.
levels.advanced: Understand where evidence supports specific effects and where it doesn't, and treat intense protocols with appropriate caution and safety rules.

name: Hormonal health
blurb: Understanding hormonal systems, testing, and treatment well enough to have a useful conversation with a doctor.

levels.beginner: Learn what the major hormones do, which symptoms actually warrant testing, and why single readings are often over-interpreted.
levels.intermediate: Understand common conditions and their standard treatments, how lifestyle factors genuinely influence hormonal health, and reference-range nuance.
levels.advanced: Engage with the clinical literature on replacement therapies and their risk profiles, and recognise the commercial incentives in the online hormone-optimisation space.

name: Meditation practice
blurb: Building an actual sitting practice, with a clear-eyed view of what it does and doesn't deliver.

levels.beginner: Learn one technique and practise short sessions daily. Expect a wandering mind — noticing it is the practice, not a failure of it.
levels.intermediate: Develop stability of attention, work with difficult mental states rather than avoiding them, and choose between concentration and insight approaches deliberately.
levels.advanced: Engage with longer retreat practice, the traditional maps and their claims, and the documented risks of intensive practice for some practitioners.

name: Public speaking
blurb: Delivering a talk that holds attention and lands its point, including the voice that carries it.

levels.beginner: Get reps in low-stakes settings and learn basic structure. Work on breath support and articulation, and listen back to your own recorded voice enough times to stop flinching at it.
levels.intermediate: Work on structure that earns attention, deliberate use of pause and pace, and handling questions and disruption without losing the thread.
levels.advanced: Develop range across formats and room sizes, adapt live to an audience that is not responding as expected, and build the vocal stamina to hold a large room without a microphone.

name: Storytelling
blurb: Structuring true stories so they hold attention and make a point, in talks, writing, or conversation.

levels.beginner: Learn basic story shape — situation, complication, turn — and practise cutting the setup that feels necessary to you but bores the listener.
levels.intermediate: Work on specificity, stakes, and scene versus summary, and learn to find the actual story inside a rambling real experience.
levels.advanced: Develop your own voice and structural instincts, handle complex or ethically delicate material, and shape stories for different media and lengths.

name: Conversation skills
blurb: Starting, sustaining, and ending conversations so both people leave them glad they happened.

levels.beginner: Learn openers that work, how to ask questions that give the other person something to answer, and how to tolerate a short silence.
levels.intermediate: Move past interview-mode: contribute your own material, notice threads worth following, and calibrate depth and disclosure to the setting.
levels.advanced: Handle groups, difficult or dominating participants, and cross-cultural differences, and steer conversations toward substance without it feeling like an agenda.

name: Body language
blurb: Understanding nonverbal behaviour honestly, including how much of the popular claims are overstated.

levels.beginner: Work on your own basics — open posture, adequate eye contact, gestures that match your words — rather than trying to read other people.
levels.intermediate: Understand clusters and baselines instead of single-cue interpretation, and adapt to context and culture rather than applying universal rules.
levels.advanced: Engage with the research critically: much popular body-language content, especially lie-detection claims, is not supported by evidence.

name: Active listening
blurb: Listening in a way that makes the other person feel accurately understood, not just heard out.

levels.beginner: Stop preparing your reply while they speak. Practise reflecting back what you heard and checking it before responding.
levels.intermediate: Learn to listen for what's under the content — the concern or need driving it — and to hold back advice until it's actually wanted.
levels.advanced: Sustain genuine listening under disagreement or personal criticism, and use it in high-stakes settings without it becoming a technique the other person can feel.

name: Negotiation
blurb: Reaching agreements that hold, by understanding interests and leverage rather than out-talking people.

levels.beginner: Learn preparation basics: your alternative if there's no deal, the other side's likely interests, and the difference between positions and interests.
levels.intermediate: Practise questioning and framing, managing concessions, and staying in a conversation that's become tense without conceding to end the discomfort.
levels.advanced: Handle multi-party and repeated negotiations, coalitions, and situations where relationship value outweighs the immediate terms.

name: Difficult conversations
blurb: Raising the thing you've been avoiding, in a way that has a chance of going well.

levels.beginner: Learn to open with the actual issue rather than a long preamble, and to separate what happened from the story you built about why.
levels.intermediate: Manage your own reactivity mid-conversation, handle defensiveness without escalating, and keep the goal in view when the other person goes sideways.
levels.advanced: Handle conversations with real power imbalance or genuine stakes, and know when a conversation is not the right instrument at all.

name: Persuasion
blurb: Changing minds with argument, framing, and evidence, and understanding where influence tips into manipulation.

levels.beginner: Learn why arguing facts harder usually fails, and start with understanding the other position well enough to state it fairly.
levels.intermediate: Work with framing, credible messengers, and reducing the social cost of changing one's mind, plus structuring an argument for a specific audience.
levels.advanced: Understand the research on persuasion and its replication problems, and hold an explicit ethical line between persuasion and exploitation.

name: Professional networking
blurb: Building useful professional relationships without transactional awkwardness or collecting contacts you never speak to.

levels.beginner: Start with people adjacent to you rather than strangers at the top, and learn how to ask for something small and specific.
levels.intermediate: Build a habit of giving value before asking, follow up in a way that isn't a chore, and use events and online communities deliberately.
levels.advanced: Maintain a wide network without it consuming your week, make useful introductions, and navigate the reciprocity dynamics of senior relationships.

name: Charisma and presence
blurb: Being someone people attend to and trust, through warmth and steadiness rather than performance.

levels.beginner: Work on the basics of presence: attention on the other person, a settled body, and not rushing your speech to fill space.
levels.intermediate: Balance warmth and competence deliberately, and develop the ability to hold a room's attention without raising your volume or status-signalling.
levels.advanced: Adapt presence across contexts and cultures, and keep it grounded in something real rather than becoming a persona you can't sustain.

name: Giving feedback
blurb: Telling someone something useful about their work in a way they can actually act on.

levels.beginner: Be specific and behavioural rather than characterological, and separate observation from interpretation before you open your mouth.
levels.intermediate: Time feedback well, make it two-way, and learn how to deliver genuinely critical feedback without either softening it into vagueness or crushing the person.
levels.advanced: Build a feedback culture rather than an event, handle feedback across power differences, and take critical feedback yourself without defensiveness.

name: Debate and argumentation
blurb: Constructing and stress-testing arguments, and disagreeing productively rather than to win.

levels.beginner: Learn argument structure, common fallacies, and the discipline of stating the other side's view so well they'd endorse it.
levels.intermediate: Practise formal or structured debate, handle burden of proof and evidence quality, and separate rhetorical wins from being right.
levels.advanced: Engage with genuinely hard disagreements where both sides have real arguments, and recognise when debate is the wrong tool for the question.

name: Resume and CV writing
blurb: Writing a document that gets you into the interview, calibrated to how it's actually screened.

levels.beginner: Get the structure and formatting right, lead with outcomes rather than duties, and cut everything that doesn't serve the specific role.
levels.intermediate: Tailor per application, quantify results honestly, and handle gaps, short tenures, or a non-linear path without apology or evasion.
levels.advanced: Position for senior or specialist roles where the document is one part of a wider case, and write for referral rather than cold application.

name: Job interviewing
blurb: Preparing for and performing in interviews so your actual competence comes across under pressure.

levels.beginner: Prepare concrete examples in a clear structure, research the company properly, and practise out loud rather than only in your head.
levels.intermediate: Handle behavioural and case questions, ask questions that reveal what the job is actually like, and manage nerves in a multi-stage process.
levels.advanced: Interview for senior roles where you're assessed on judgement and stakeholder handling, and evaluate the employer as seriously as they evaluate you.

name: Salary negotiation
blurb: Negotiating pay and terms with the leverage and market information you actually have.

levels.beginner: Learn to research market rates, avoid naming a number first when you can, and ask for time before responding to an offer.
levels.intermediate: Negotiate the full package rather than base alone, build a documented case for a raise, and handle the conversation without threatening to leave.
levels.advanced: Handle competing offers, equity and complex compensation structures, and negotiations where the relationship continues long after the number is settled.

name: Changing careers
blurb: Moving into a different field deliberately, including how to test a direction before committing to it.

levels.beginner: Investigate before you leap: talk to people doing the work, and test the day-to-day reality rather than the idea of the job.
levels.intermediate: Build a bridge — transferable framing, side projects, or an adjacent internal move — and plan the financial runway realistically.
levels.advanced: Manage a senior-level change where you're taking a title or pay step back, and rebuild credibility in a field where your track record doesn't transfer.

name: Leadership
blurb: Setting direction and building trust so a group does good work without you managing every detail.

levels.beginner: Learn the shift from doing to enabling: clarity of direction, consistency, and the fact that your behaviour sets the standard whether you intend it or not.
levels.intermediate: Build trust and psychological safety deliberately, communicate strategy so it's actionable, and handle underperformance without avoidance.
levels.advanced: Lead through other leaders, hold a direction through uncertainty and bad news, and make decisions where every option has real costs.

name: Managing people
blurb: The practical craft of one-to-ones, performance, hiring, and difficult personnel decisions.

levels.beginner: Run useful one-to-ones, set clear expectations, and resist the pull to keep doing the individual contributor work you were good at.
levels.intermediate: Handle performance problems early and fairly, develop people toward what they want, and manage across differing levels of experience.
levels.advanced: Manage managers, handle restructures and terminations humanely, and build a team that performs without your constant presence.

name: Remote work
blurb: Working effectively at a distance — communication, visibility, and keeping work from filling the day.

levels.beginner: Set up a workable space and routine, and learn to communicate in writing with enough context that no follow-up call is needed.
levels.intermediate: Work asynchronously on purpose, make your work visible without performing busyness, and protect boundaries between work and home.
levels.advanced: Lead distributed teams across time zones, build culture without proximity, and handle the career risks of being remote in a hybrid organisation.

name: Business writing
blurb: Writing documents, updates, and emails that are clear, short, and get a decision made.

levels.beginner: Lead with the point, cut hedging and filler, and learn basic structure so the reader knows what you want from them in the first line.
levels.intermediate: Write proposals and decision documents that survive being read out of context, and adapt register for different audiences and seniority.
levels.advanced: Write for organisational decision-making at scale — strategy documents, narrative memos — where the writing shapes what gets decided.

name: Running meetings
blurb: Running meetings that make decisions, and cancelling the ones that shouldn't exist.

levels.beginner: Write an agenda with a purpose and a decision to be made, and finish with owners and next steps rather than a vague sense of agreement.
levels.intermediate: Manage participation actively — draw out the quiet, contain the dominant — and use structured formats for decisions and brainstorming.
levels.advanced: Facilitate high-stakes or contentious sessions, design workshops that produce real output, and handle group dynamics you didn't create.

name: Freelancing
blurb: Running solo client work: finding clients, pricing, contracts, and keeping a pipeline that doesn't collapse.

levels.beginner: Define a specific service and who it's for, set a rate that covers non-billable time, and use a written contract from the first client.
levels.intermediate: Build a repeatable pipeline rather than relying on referrals, handle scope creep and late payment, and raise rates with existing clients.
levels.advanced: Move up-market to fewer, larger clients, productise your offer, and manage the feast-and-famine cycle and the tax and admin load.

name: Consulting
blurb: Selling and delivering expertise as engagements, with the diagnosis and framing as the real value.

levels.beginner: Learn the difference between doing the work and advising on it, and how to run a first discovery conversation that surfaces the real problem.
levels.intermediate: Structure engagements and proposals, price on value rather than hours, and manage stakeholders who disagree with each other about the goal.
levels.advanced: Build a practice with repeatable methodology and referral flow, and handle engagements where the recommendation is politically unwelcome.

name: Workplace politics
blurb: Reading organisational power and incentives accurately, and operating in them without becoming cynical.

levels.beginner: Learn to see how decisions actually get made in your organisation, and stop assuming good work speaks for itself.
levels.intermediate: Build influence without authority, manage upward deliberately, and handle credit, blame, and visibility fairly.
levels.advanced: Operate at levels where resource allocation is genuinely contested, and decide when a political environment is one you should leave.

name: Delegation
blurb: Handing work over so it's genuinely off your plate and the other person grows from it.

levels.beginner: Delegate outcomes with context rather than step-by-step instructions, and accept that a different method producing the result is fine.
levels.intermediate: Match the level of autonomy to the person and the risk, set check-ins that aren't micromanagement, and delegate work you enjoy, not only work you dislike.
levels.advanced: Build capability deliberately across a team so delegation scales, and handle the cases where delegated work genuinely goes wrong.

name: Personal budgeting
blurb: Knowing where your money goes and directing it on purpose, with a system you'll actually maintain.

levels.beginner: Track actual spending for a month before designing anything, then set up a simple system — automated transfers beat manual discipline.
levels.intermediate: Build sinking funds for irregular costs, handle variable income, and adjust the budget when it repeatedly fails rather than blaming yourself.
levels.advanced: Integrate budgeting with longer-term goals and tax-aware saving, and manage household finances jointly where incomes and habits differ.

name: Getting out of debt
blurb: Paying down consumer debt with a method that matches both the maths and your psychology.

levels.beginner: List every debt with its rate and minimum, stop adding to the balance, and pick one payoff order and stick with it.
levels.intermediate: Weigh refinancing and consolidation properly, negotiate with creditors, and balance debt payoff against an emergency buffer and employer match.
levels.advanced: Handle serious debt situations, understand the legal and credit consequences of the harder options, and rebuild afterwards.

name: Index fund investing
blurb: Building a low-cost, diversified long-term portfolio and then mostly leaving it alone.

levels.beginner: Understand diversification, fees, and the tax-advantaged accounts available to you, then automate contributions into a simple allocation.
levels.intermediate: Set an asset allocation you can hold through a drawdown, rebalance on a rule, and understand tax placement across account types.
levels.advanced: Handle withdrawal strategy, sequence-of-returns risk, and the evidence on factor tilts and international allocation without over-engineering.

name: Analysing individual stocks
blurb: Reading financial statements and valuing a business, with clear eyes about how hard beating the market is.

levels.beginner: Learn to read the three financial statements and what the common ratios actually mean before forming an opinion on any company.
levels.intermediate: Build a valuation from cash flows, understand competitive position and capital allocation, and write down a thesis you can later be wrong about.
levels.advanced: Handle cyclicals, accounting complexity, and position sizing, and honestly benchmark your results against a passive alternative.

name: Retirement planning
blurb: Working out what you'll need, what you're on track for, and which account structures to use.

levels.beginner: Capture any employer match, understand your available account types, and start contributing before optimising the details.
levels.intermediate: Model a target number with realistic assumptions, understand contribution limits and tax treatment, and adjust for career changes.
levels.advanced: Plan the decumulation phase — withdrawal order, tax efficiency, healthcare, and longevity risk — rather than only the accumulation side.

name: Tax basics
blurb: Understanding how your income is actually taxed and which legitimate reliefs apply to you.

levels.beginner: Learn marginal versus effective rates, what's withheld, and which reliefs and allowances you're already entitled to.
levels.intermediate: Handle self-employment and side income, understand deductible expenses properly, and plan estimated payments to avoid year-end shocks.
levels.advanced: Coordinate tax across investments, business structure, and retirement accounts, and know the point at which a professional pays for themselves.

name: Real estate investing
blurb: Evaluating property as an investment on numbers rather than narrative, including the work it actually involves.

levels.beginner: Learn to underwrite a deal honestly — including vacancy, maintenance, and management — before believing any advertised yield.
levels.intermediate: Handle financing, tenant selection, and the legal obligations of a landlord, and understand the real time cost of self-managing.
levels.advanced: Scale into multi-unit or commercial property, manage leverage risk through a downturn, and evaluate syndications and partnerships critically.

name: Credit and loans
blurb: Understanding how credit is scored and priced, and borrowing on terms that don't quietly cost you.

levels.beginner: Learn what actually affects a credit score, how to check yours, and how to read the total cost of a loan rather than the monthly payment.
levels.intermediate: Compare mortgage and loan structures properly, understand fixed versus variable risk, and use credit deliberately rather than reactively.
levels.advanced: Handle refinancing decisions, credit repair after damage, and borrowing structured around investment or business rather than consumption.

name: Crypto literacy
blurb: Understanding how these systems technically work, and the risk and fraud landscape around them.

levels.beginner: Understand what a blockchain actually is, custody and key management, and the most common scam patterns before putting money anywhere.
levels.intermediate: Learn how specific protocols work technically, the difference between a token's mechanism and its marketing, and self-custody practices.
levels.advanced: Engage with the serious critiques as well as the technology, understand regulatory and counterparty risk, and size exposure accordingly.

name: Financial independence
blurb: Building enough invested assets to make work optional, and thinking clearly about what that's for.

levels.beginner: Understand the arithmetic of savings rate and time to independence, and start increasing the gap between income and spending.
levels.intermediate: Model withdrawal rates with their assumptions and failure modes, and plan healthcare, taxes, and the transition years.
levels.advanced: Handle decumulation in practice, sequence risk, and the identity and purpose questions that arrive once the number is reached.

name: Insurance basics
blurb: Buying the cover you actually need against ruinous risks, and skipping the products that mainly benefit the seller.

levels.beginner: Learn what insurance is for — catastrophic risk, not small costs — and identify which policies your situation genuinely requires.
levels.intermediate: Compare policies on exclusions and claim behaviour rather than premium alone, and get the sums insured right for dependants and liabilities.
levels.advanced: Understand complex products and where investment and insurance are bundled unfavourably, and coordinate cover with your wider financial plan.

name: Psychology of money
blurb: Understanding the emotional and cognitive patterns that drive financial decisions more than spreadsheets do.

levels.beginner: Notice your own money patterns and where they came from, and learn the common errors: panic selling, chasing performance, lifestyle creep.
levels.intermediate: Build decision rules and automation that remove emotion at the moments it costs most, and understand risk tolerance as behaviour rather than a questionnaire.
levels.advanced: Engage with the research and its limits, and work on the deeper relationship between money, security, and status that drives the decisions.

name: Startup fundamentals
blurb: Finding a problem worth solving and testing whether anyone will actually pay for your solution.

levels.beginner: Talk to potential customers before building. Learn to hear what people do rather than what they say they'd do, and define the problem precisely.
levels.intermediate: Run real experiments toward product-market fit, choose a first channel deliberately, and know which metrics distinguish traction from noise.
levels.advanced: Handle the transition from finding a market to scaling into it, including hiring, focus, and the strategic choices that close off other options.

name: Bootstrapping a business
blurb: Building a profitable business from revenue rather than investment, and keeping it sustainable solo or small.

levels.beginner: Pick something you can sell early and cheaply to build, and get to first revenue rather than perfecting the product in private.
levels.intermediate: Grow through repeatable acquisition you can afford, price for profitability, and resist scope creep that turns a small business into a job you hate.
levels.advanced: Scale without outside capital: hire carefully, build systems that survive your absence, and decide deliberately between growth and staying small.

name: Running a SaaS business
blurb: The specific mechanics of subscription software: retention, expansion, and the metrics that actually predict survival.

levels.beginner: Understand the core loop — acquisition, activation, retention — and why churn quietly kills subscription businesses that look like they're growing.
levels.intermediate: Work cohort retention, expansion revenue, and payback period, and build onboarding that gets users to value fast.
levels.advanced: Handle enterprise motion, multi-product expansion, and unit economics under different growth strategies and funding structures.

name: Ecommerce
blurb: Selling physical products online: sourcing, margins, logistics, and acquisition that doesn't eat the profit.

levels.beginner: Understand landed cost and true margin before choosing a product, and get one channel and one product working before adding either.
levels.intermediate: Manage inventory and cash cycle, improve conversion and average order value, and diversify acquisition beyond a single ad platform.
levels.advanced: Handle multi-channel operations, brand building versus performance marketing, and the working-capital constraints that limit growth.

name: Venture fundraising
blurb: Raising investment: what investors are underwriting, how terms work, and whether you should raise at all.

levels.beginner: Understand what venture capital is for and the growth expectations it imposes, and whether your business is a fit for it.
levels.intermediate: Build a narrative and deck that survives scrutiny, run a process rather than one-off conversations, and understand dilution and basic terms.
levels.advanced: Negotiate terms with real consequence — liquidation preferences, board composition, control — and manage investors after the round closes.

name: Business strategy
blurb: Choosing where to compete and what not to do, in a way that survives contact with competitors.

levels.beginner: Learn that strategy is choice and sacrifice, not a list of goals, and analyse your market's actual structure and competitors.
levels.intermediate: Work with positioning, cost and differentiation trade-offs, and durable advantage, and translate strategy into resource allocation.
levels.advanced: Handle strategy under real uncertainty, adjacent market entry, and the organisational politics of killing a profitable but strategically wrong line.

name: Pricing
blurb: Setting prices based on value and willingness to pay rather than cost-plus or competitor-matching.

levels.beginner: Stop pricing off costs alone. Learn to research willingness to pay and understand what your price signals about the product.
levels.intermediate: Design packaging and tiers, choose value metrics that scale with customer benefit, and run price increases without losing the base.
levels.advanced: Handle segmentation and discounting discipline, price complex or multi-product offers, and test pricing changes without damaging trust.

name: Hiring
blurb: Designing a hiring process that predicts performance rather than rewarding interview skill.

levels.beginner: Define the role and the actual signals of success before writing the ad, and use structured interviews rather than unstructured conversation.
levels.intermediate: Build work-sample assessments, calibrate interviewers, and manage the candidate experience and offer stage well.
levels.advanced: Hire senior and specialist roles, build a pipeline rather than reacting to vacancies, and measure the quality of your own hiring decisions over time.

name: Operations and process
blurb: Building the repeatable systems that let a business deliver consistently without heroics.

levels.beginner: Document what you actually do before trying to improve it, and start with the process whose failure costs you most.
levels.intermediate: Map and improve workflows, remove bottlenecks rather than local inefficiencies, and build handoffs that don't rely on memory.
levels.advanced: Design operations that scale with headcount and volume, and balance standardisation against the flexibility the work genuinely needs.

name: Small business finance
blurb: Reading your own numbers — cash flow, margin, and runway — well enough to make decisions with them.

levels.beginner: Separate business and personal money, keep books from day one, and learn to read a profit and loss statement and a cash flow forecast.
levels.intermediate: Understand margin by product or client, manage working capital and payment terms, and forecast well enough to see problems early.
levels.advanced: Handle financing decisions, unit economics under growth, and the financial modelling behind hiring, pricing, and investment choices.

name: Product management
blurb: Deciding what to build and why, and getting a team to a shipped outcome that users adopt.

levels.beginner: Learn discovery: talking to users, defining the problem, and writing requirements that describe outcomes rather than features.
levels.intermediate: Prioritise with explicit trade-offs, work effectively with engineering and design, and measure whether shipped work moved anything.
levels.advanced: Own strategy for a product area, manage stakeholders with conflicting goals, and make bets whose payoff is a year out.

name: Buying a business
blurb: Acquiring an existing small business: sourcing deals, valuing them, and doing real diligence.

levels.beginner: Understand why owners sell, what a small business is actually worth, and the basic deal structures before looking at listings.
levels.intermediate: Run financial and operational diligence, structure financing including seller notes, and plan the ownership transition honestly.
levels.advanced: Handle competitive processes, complex structures and earn-outs, and the post-acquisition work where most value is won or lost.

name: Legal basics for founders
blurb: Understanding entities, contracts, and IP well enough to ask a lawyer the right questions.

levels.beginner: Learn entity types and what they protect, why founder agreements and vesting exist, and which contracts you must never sign unread.
levels.intermediate: Understand customer and supplier contract terms that carry real risk, IP assignment, and basic employment and contractor distinctions.
levels.advanced: Handle investment documents, licensing, and disputes, and know where jurisdiction-specific advice is not optional.

name: Copywriting
blurb: Writing words that sell — clear, specific, and built on research rather than clever phrasing.

levels.beginner: Learn that copy starts with customer research, not writing. Practise clear headlines, specific benefits, and cutting everything that doesn't move the reader.
levels.intermediate: Structure long-form sales pages, handle objections in sequence, and write for a defined awareness stage rather than everyone at once.
levels.advanced: Develop voice and offer positioning, test systematically, and write across formats where the constraint differs sharply.

name: Search engine optimisation
blurb: Earning search traffic through content, technical health, and links, in an environment that keeps changing.

levels.beginner: Understand how search works, do basic keyword research, and fix the technical and on-page issues that block indexing.
levels.intermediate: Build topical depth rather than isolated posts, earn links legitimately, and diagnose traffic changes against algorithm updates.
levels.advanced: Handle large-site technical SEO, international and ecommerce complexity, and adapt strategy as AI-generated answers change click behaviour.

name: Content marketing
blurb: Building an audience with useful content and connecting it to a business outcome rather than vanity metrics.

levels.beginner: Choose a specific audience and topic, publish consistently, and learn to write something genuinely more useful than what already ranks.
levels.intermediate: Build a content strategy tied to a funnel, repurpose across channels deliberately, and measure contribution rather than pageviews.
levels.advanced: Run content as a portfolio with editorial standards, manage writers, and sustain distribution as channels decline or shift.

name: Email marketing
blurb: Building a list people want to be on and sending emails that get opened, read, and acted on.

levels.beginner: Set up a list with a clear promise, write a welcome sequence, and send regularly enough that people remember subscribing.
levels.intermediate: Segment meaningfully, build automated sequences tied to behaviour, and manage deliverability rather than assuming it works.
levels.advanced: Run lifecycle programmes at scale, test structurally rather than on subject lines alone, and balance revenue emails against list health.

name: Cold email outreach
blurb: Writing cold emails that get replies, and running outreach that stays legal and doesn't burn your domain.

levels.beginner: Research a narrow list, write short specific emails referencing something real, and understand the legal rules for your recipients' jurisdictions.
levels.intermediate: Build repeatable sequences with genuine personalisation at scale, manage sending infrastructure and deliverability, and measure reply quality not volume.
levels.advanced: Run outbound as a system with clear targeting and qualification, and know when outbound is the wrong channel for your offer entirely.

name: Paid advertising
blurb: Buying traffic profitably across ad platforms, with measurement you can actually trust.

levels.beginner: Understand auction mechanics and the basic account structure, and set up conversion tracking before spending meaningful money.
levels.intermediate: Work creative testing, audience strategy, and bidding, and learn to read results at a statistically sensible sample size.
levels.advanced: Manage significant budgets across channels, handle incrementality and attribution honestly, and build creative pipelines that keep pace with fatigue.

name: Social media growth
blurb: Growing an audience on social platforms without mistaking follower count for a business.

levels.beginner: Pick one platform and one format, post consistently, and study what performs in your niche rather than copying generic advice.
levels.intermediate: Develop a repeatable content system, understand each platform's distribution mechanics, and convert attention into email or revenue.
levels.advanced: Manage a multi-platform presence and a team, handle platform dependency risk, and sustain output without burning out.

name: Brand strategy
blurb: Deciding what you want to stand for in a customer's mind, and making everything consistent with it.

levels.beginner: Learn that brand is positioning plus consistency, not a logo. Define who you're for and what you're the alternative to.
levels.intermediate: Build messaging architecture and verbal identity, and align visual identity with the positioning rather than with taste.
levels.advanced: Manage brand at scale across products and markets, handle repositioning, and measure brand effects that don't show in last-click reporting.

name: Sales fundamentals
blurb: Running a sales conversation that qualifies honestly and helps the buyer make a decision either way.

levels.beginner: Learn discovery: ask questions that surface the actual problem and its cost, and get comfortable disqualifying people who aren't a fit.
levels.intermediate: Manage a pipeline and a multi-stakeholder process, handle objections as information, and forecast without wishful thinking.
levels.advanced: Run complex enterprise cycles, build and coach a sales process others can execute, and hold pricing discipline under pressure.

name: Conversion optimisation
blurb: Improving the percentage of visitors who act, using research and tests rather than redesign hunches.

levels.beginner: Learn where users actually drop off before changing anything, and fix the obvious clarity and friction problems first.
levels.intermediate: Run valid A/B tests with adequate sample size, form hypotheses from research, and avoid the traps of peeking and multiple comparisons.
levels.advanced: Build a testing programme with prioritisation and knowledge capture, and know when traffic volume makes testing the wrong approach.

name: Marketing analytics
blurb: Measuring what marketing actually caused, and being honest about attribution's limits.

levels.beginner: Get clean tracking and a small set of metrics that matter, and learn what standard reports do and don't tell you.
levels.intermediate: Understand attribution models and their assumptions, build cohort and channel reporting, and connect marketing data to revenue.
levels.advanced: Use incrementality testing and modelling to estimate causal effect, and communicate uncertainty to stakeholders who want a single number.

name: Affiliate marketing
blurb: Earning commission by recommending products, with disclosure and trust as the constraint that makes it viable.

levels.beginner: Understand the model and the disclosure rules, and choose products you'd recommend without the commission.
levels.intermediate: Build content that ranks or converts for purchase-intent audiences, and negotiate rates once you have proven volume.
levels.advanced: Run affiliate as a business with diversified programmes and traffic sources, and manage the conflict between commission and honest recommendation.

name: Community building
blurb: Creating a space where members talk to each other, not just to you, and moderating it well.

levels.beginner: Define why the community exists and for whom, and seed early conversation manually rather than waiting for activity to appear.
levels.intermediate: Develop norms and moderation, create rituals and recurring formats, and build a core of members who contribute without prompting.
levels.advanced: Scale governance and moderation, handle conflict and toxicity, and sustain a community through platform changes and founder step-back.

name: Prompt engineering
blurb: Getting reliable results from language models through structure, context, and systematic iteration.

levels.beginner: Learn to give context, examples, and an explicit output format, and to iterate on a prompt rather than accepting the first response.
levels.intermediate: Use structured techniques deliberately, decompose tasks into steps, and build evaluation sets so you know whether a change helped.
levels.advanced: Design prompts as part of a system with retrieval and tools, handle failure modes and adversarial input, and measure reliability rather than eyeballing outputs.

name: AI fundamentals
blurb: Understanding how modern machine learning systems actually work, well enough to judge claims about them.

levels.beginner: Understand what training and inference are, what a model is doing when it predicts, and why these systems fail in the ways they do.
levels.intermediate: Learn the architectures and training methods behind current systems, and read papers and benchmarks with appropriate scepticism.
levels.advanced: Engage with current research directions, evaluation methodology, and the open questions about capability and interpretability.

name: Building with LLMs
blurb: Turning language models into working applications: retrieval, tools, evaluation, and cost control.

levels.beginner: Build something small end to end with an API, and learn where model output needs validation before it touches anything real.
levels.intermediate: Implement retrieval, tool use, and structured output, and build evaluation harnesses instead of testing by vibes.
levels.advanced: Design for reliability, latency, and cost at scale, handle security concerns like prompt injection, and know when a model is the wrong component.

name: AI ethics and risk
blurb: Thinking clearly about the harms, incentives, and governance questions around AI systems.

levels.beginner: Learn the documented, present-day harms — bias, labour, misinformation, environmental cost — separately from speculative future scenarios.
levels.intermediate: Understand the technical basis of these problems, the main regulatory approaches, and the disagreements between research communities.
levels.advanced: Engage seriously with competing frameworks, evaluate governance proposals on mechanism rather than sentiment, and separate research from positioning.

name: Cybersecurity basics
blurb: Protecting your accounts, devices, and data against the attacks that actually happen to ordinary people.

levels.beginner: Get a password manager, turn on multi-factor authentication, and learn to recognise phishing. This covers most realistic risk.
levels.intermediate: Understand common attack classes and defences, secure your home and work setup, and think in terms of a threat model rather than a checklist.
levels.advanced: Study offensive and defensive technique properly, understand incident response, and keep a clear ethical and legal line around testing.

name: Privacy and operational security
blurb: Reducing how much of your life is collected and linkable, with effort proportionate to your actual threat model.

levels.beginner: Understand who collects what and why, then take the high-value steps: browser and account hygiene, and reducing needless data sharing.
levels.intermediate: Build a threat model, compartmentalise identities and services, and evaluate privacy tools by what they actually protect against.
levels.advanced: Handle higher-risk situations properly, understand metadata and correlation attacks, and accept the usability trade-offs honestly.

name: Home networking
blurb: Understanding and building a home network that's fast, reliable, and reasonably secure.

levels.beginner: Learn what your router actually does, place and configure wireless properly, and secure the network with basics rather than defaults.
levels.intermediate: Work with VLANs, wired backhaul, DNS, and remote access, and diagnose problems with real tools instead of rebooting hopefully.
levels.advanced: Design segmented networks with proper firewalling, run your own DNS and VPN infrastructure, and manage a network with many devices reliably.

name: Self-hosting
blurb: Running your own services on your own hardware, and accepting the maintenance that comes with it.

levels.beginner: Start with one service on modest hardware, learn containers, and set up backups before you have data you'd miss.
levels.intermediate: Run several services with reverse proxying and certificates, expose things safely, and automate updates and monitoring.
levels.advanced: Build resilient storage and backup strategies, handle authentication across services, and manage a homelab without it becoming a second job.

name: Linux and the command line
blurb: Working comfortably in a shell and understanding how a Linux system is put together.

levels.beginner: Learn navigation, files and permissions, package management, and enough shell to stop being afraid of the terminal.
levels.intermediate: Write useful scripts, understand processes, services, and networking basics, and troubleshoot from logs rather than reinstalling.
levels.advanced: Understand the system deeply — init, filesystems, kernel interfaces — and administer machines with configuration you can reproduce.

name: Building a PC
blurb: Choosing components that suit what you actually do, assembling them, and diagnosing when it doesn't post.

levels.beginner: Learn what each component does and how they must match, then build to a budget around your actual workload rather than benchmarks alone.
levels.intermediate: Handle cooling, power, and airflow properly, understand real-world performance bottlenecks, and troubleshoot boot and stability problems.
levels.advanced: Tune and undervolt sensibly, build for specialised workloads, and evaluate hardware claims against independent testing methodology.

name: Data literacy
blurb: Reading charts, statistics, and studies critically enough to notice when the number isn't saying what it seems to.

levels.beginner: Learn to read a chart properly — axes, base rates, sample — and to ask what's being compared and what's been left out.
levels.intermediate: Understand distributions, uncertainty, confounding, and correlation versus causation well enough to evaluate a typical published claim.
levels.advanced: Assess study design and statistical methodology, understand replication and publication bias, and communicate uncertainty honestly.

name: Python programming
blurb: Learning Python properly — the language, its idioms, and the ecosystem you'll actually use.

levels.beginner: Learn syntax, data structures, and functions by building small programs. Type the code yourself rather than watching someone else type it.
levels.intermediate: Write idiomatic Python: comprehensions, generators, context managers, and modules structured for reuse, plus virtual environments and packaging.
levels.advanced: Understand the runtime — the object model, concurrency options, and performance characteristics — and know when Python is the wrong tool.

name: JavaScript
blurb: Learning the language of the web well, including the asynchronous model that trips most people up.

levels.beginner: Learn values, functions, objects, and the DOM, and build small interactive pages before touching any framework.
levels.intermediate: Understand closures, prototypes, modules, and asynchronous flow with promises, plus the tooling and type checking most codebases assume.
levels.advanced: Understand the event loop and engine behaviour, performance and memory characteristics, and the trade-offs behind framework design.

name: Frontend web development
blurb: Building interfaces in the browser: HTML semantics, CSS layout, accessibility, and component frameworks.

levels.beginner: Learn semantic HTML and CSS layout with flexbox and grid, and build responsive pages without a framework first.
levels.intermediate: Work with a component framework, manage state deliberately, and take accessibility and performance seriously rather than as an afterthought.
levels.advanced: Handle rendering strategies, large-application architecture, and performance budgets, and evaluate framework choices on real constraints.

name: Backend development
blurb: Building the server side: APIs, data access, authentication, and the reliability concerns behind them.

levels.beginner: Build a small API with a database behind it, and understand the request lifecycle from route to query to response.
levels.intermediate: Handle authentication, validation, background jobs, and error handling properly, and structure a codebase that stays workable as it grows.
levels.advanced: Design for concurrency, consistency, and failure, and make architectural choices with an honest view of operational cost.

name: Databases and SQL
blurb: Modelling data well and querying it efficiently, in relational systems and where they're not the answer.

levels.beginner: Learn SQL for real queries — joins, aggregation, filtering — and basic schema design with sensible keys and types.
levels.intermediate: Understand indexing, query plans, transactions, and normalisation trade-offs, and diagnose slow queries rather than guessing.
levels.advanced: Handle scaling, replication, and consistency models, and choose between relational and other stores based on access patterns.

name: DevOps and CI/CD
blurb: Automating build, test, and deployment so shipping is routine rather than an event.

levels.beginner: Set up a pipeline that builds and tests on every change, and containerise an application so it runs the same everywhere.
levels.intermediate: Automate deployment with rollback, manage configuration and secrets properly, and add monitoring and alerting that people act on.
levels.advanced: Design infrastructure as code at scale, handle orchestration and progressive delivery, and treat reliability as an engineering discipline.

name: Cloud computing
blurb: Using cloud platforms competently — the core services, the pricing model, and the lock-in questions.

levels.beginner: Learn the core primitives — compute, storage, networking, identity — and deploy something small while watching what it costs.
levels.intermediate: Design with managed services appropriately, secure access with least privilege, and control spend before the bill teaches you.
levels.advanced: Architect for availability and cost at scale, handle multi-region and data residency, and evaluate portability against operational simplicity.

name: System design
blurb: Designing systems that meet real requirements at scale, and explaining the trade-offs you chose.

levels.beginner: Learn the building blocks — load balancing, caching, queues, replication — and what each one costs as well as what it solves.
levels.intermediate: Practise designing complete systems from requirements, reason about bottlenecks quantitatively, and handle failure modes explicitly.
levels.advanced: Work with consistency trade-offs, distributed coordination, and evolutionary architecture for systems that already exist and can't stop running.

name: Algorithms and data structures
blurb: Building the problem-solving foundation that makes hard programming problems tractable and interviews survivable.

levels.beginner: Learn arrays, hash maps, and basic complexity analysis, and solve easy problems by hand before coding them.
levels.intermediate: Work through trees, graphs, recursion, and dynamic programming with deliberate practice on patterns rather than problem count.
levels.advanced: Handle harder algorithmic topics and optimisation, and know when an elegant algorithm is worse than a straightforward one in production.

name: Git and version control
blurb: Using Git with an actual mental model, so branching and history stop being frightening.

levels.beginner: Learn the staging area, commits, branches, and remotes, and how to write a commit message someone can use later.
levels.intermediate: Handle merges and rebases confidently, resolve conflicts, and recover from mistakes with reflog rather than recloning.
levels.advanced: Understand Git's object model, design branching workflows for a team, and use bisect and history rewriting responsibly.

name: Testing and code quality
blurb: Writing tests that catch real problems and code that the next person can safely change.

levels.beginner: Write unit tests for logic you own, learn what makes a test readable and deterministic, and run them automatically.
levels.intermediate: Balance the test pyramid, test at the right boundaries, and refactor with tests as a safety net rather than chasing coverage numbers.
levels.advanced: Design testable architecture, handle integration and end-to-end suites that stay fast and reliable, and lead code review as a quality practice.

name: Mobile app development
blurb: Building apps for phones — platform conventions, lifecycle, and shipping through app stores.

levels.beginner: Build a small app end to end on one platform and learn its UI framework and lifecycle rather than fighting them.
levels.intermediate: Handle state, navigation, local storage, and network reliability, and follow platform interface conventions deliberately.
levels.advanced: Manage performance, offline behaviour, and release engineering, and weigh native against cross-platform on real constraints.

name: Game development
blurb: Building games: engine work, game feel, and the scoping discipline that gets one finished.

levels.beginner: Finish a very small game in one engine. Scope is the main skill at this stage, and a finished tiny game teaches more than an abandoned big one.
levels.intermediate: Work on game feel, systems design, and performance, and learn the production side including asset pipelines and playtesting.
levels.advanced: Handle larger projects and teams, engine-level work or custom tooling, and the commercial realities of releasing and marketing a game.

name: Machine learning engineering
blurb: Training, evaluating, and deploying models as software that has to keep working in production.

levels.beginner: Learn the workflow end to end on a small dataset: features, training, validation, and why a good test set matters more than a clever model.
levels.intermediate: Handle real data pipelines, experiment tracking, and deployment, and evaluate with metrics that match the actual decision being made.
levels.advanced: Manage models in production — drift, retraining, monitoring, cost — and understand where the modelling problem is really a data problem.

name: Video editing
blurb: Cutting footage so it holds attention — pacing, sound, and story before effects.

levels.beginner: Learn one editor's basic workflow and focus on rhythm and clarity: cut the boring parts, fix the audio, and finish something.
levels.intermediate: Work on pacing, transitions with intent, colour and sound balance, and organising a project so long edits stay manageable.
