levels.advanced: Develop editorial judgement for structure and emotion, handle colour grading and finishing properly, and edit efficiently to a deadline.

name: Filmmaking
blurb: Making films: camera, lighting, sound, and directing choices that serve the story.

levels.beginner: Learn exposure, framing, and — most neglected — sound. Make short pieces with whatever camera you have rather than waiting for gear.
levels.intermediate: Work with lighting deliberately, plan coverage and blocking, and direct performance rather than only operating a camera.
levels.advanced: Develop a visual approach that serves a specific story, manage a crew and production logistics, and handle the finishing chain to delivery.

name: Photography
blurb: Making photographs that work — light, composition, and knowing your camera well enough to forget it.

levels.beginner: Learn exposure, focus, and composition, and shoot a lot in one genre. Gear matters far less than seeing light at this stage.
levels.intermediate: Develop consistency in a genre, learn editing and colour in a raw workflow, and work with artificial light when you need it.
levels.advanced: Develop a body of work with a coherent voice, handle client or documentary constraints, and print or publish to a standard.

name: Graphic design
blurb: Designing with type, hierarchy, colour, and space so a message reads clearly.

levels.beginner: Learn typography, hierarchy, alignment, and contrast, and copy good work deliberately to understand why it's structured that way.
levels.intermediate: Build systems rather than one-offs, use grids and colour with intent, and take design decisions from a brief rather than taste.
levels.advanced: Develop identity systems, art-direct across media, and defend design decisions with reasoning a client can follow.

name: UI and UX design
blurb: Designing interfaces people can use, grounded in research rather than what looks good in a portfolio shot.

levels.beginner: Learn interface patterns and why they exist, build basic wireframes, and watch a real person use something you made.
levels.intermediate: Run usability testing and research, design flows rather than screens, and work with design systems and accessibility requirements.
levels.advanced: Handle complex product problems, measure design outcomes, and work with engineering constraints and organisational realities.

name: Drawing and illustration
blurb: Learning to draw through observation and structure, whether on paper or digitally.

levels.beginner: Draw from observation regularly and learn construction, proportion, and value. Volume of practice matters more than materials.
levels.intermediate: Study anatomy, perspective, and colour deliberately, and work on finishing pieces rather than only sketching.
levels.advanced: Develop a personal style with intent, work to briefs and deadlines, and build a body of work that holds together.

name: Music production
blurb: Making finished tracks in a DAW: arrangement, sound selection, mixing, and knowing when it's done.

levels.beginner: Learn one DAW's workflow and finish short tracks. Completing bad songs teaches more than endlessly refining a single loop.
levels.intermediate: Work on arrangement, sound design, and mixing fundamentals — gain staging, EQ, compression — and reference against commercial tracks.
levels.advanced: Develop a recognisable sonic identity, handle mixing and mastering to release standard, and collaborate or produce for other artists.

name: Guitar
blurb: Learning guitar with structured practice instead of endlessly repeating what you can already play.

levels.beginner: Build chord changes, rhythm, and finger strength on real songs, and practise short and often rather than long and rarely.
levels.intermediate: Learn the fretboard and theory as it applies to playing, develop technique deliberately, and play with other people or a metronome.
levels.advanced: Work on improvisation, tone, and stylistic depth, and practise with the diagnostic precision that separates plateau from progress.

name: Piano
blurb: Learning piano with attention to technique and reading, so progress compounds rather than stalls.

levels.beginner: Build hand position, basic reading, and simple two-hand coordination on pieces slightly below your ambition level.
levels.intermediate: Develop sight-reading, scales and arpeggios with musical intent, and learn repertoire that stretches specific technical weaknesses.
levels.advanced: Work on interpretation, tone control, and performance under pressure, and practise with deliberate problem isolation rather than repetition.

name: Singing
blurb: Training your voice safely — breath, registers, and pitch — rather than straining toward a sound.

levels.beginner: Learn breath support, relaxed posture, and pitch matching, and warm up properly. Most beginner problems are tension, not talent.
levels.intermediate: Work on register transitions, resonance, and range extension without strain, and record yourself to hear what listeners hear.
levels.advanced: Develop stylistic control and stamina, handle performance and microphone technique, and protect vocal health under heavy use.

name: Creative writing
blurb: Writing fiction or narrative nonfiction: scene, voice, structure, and finishing drafts.

levels.beginner: Write regularly and finish short pieces. Learn scene versus summary and the basics of point of view before worrying about style.
levels.intermediate: Work on structure at length, character motivation, dialogue, and revision as a distinct skill from drafting.
levels.advanced: Develop a voice and handle long-form structural problems, take critique usefully, and navigate publication routes realistically.

name: Animation
blurb: Making things move convincingly — timing, spacing, and weight, in 2D or 3D.

levels.beginner: Learn timing and spacing with simple exercises like a bouncing ball before attempting characters. The principles matter more than the software.
levels.intermediate: Work on character animation and weight, learn a full pipeline in one tool, and study reference footage frame by frame.
levels.advanced: Develop performance and acting in animation, handle complex rigs or effects work, and produce to professional pipeline standards.

name: Woodworking
blurb: Building things in wood with accurate joinery, sharp tools, and safe habits.

levels.beginner: Learn measuring, marking, sawing, and sharpening on simple projects, and establish safe habits with every tool from the start.
levels.intermediate: Work on accurate joinery, wood movement, and finishing, and design projects rather than only following plans.
levels.advanced: Handle complex furniture, veneer and curved work, and shop workflow and jigs that make precision repeatable.

name: Podcasting
blurb: Making a podcast people finish: audio quality, interview skill, and a format that sustains.

levels.beginner: Get clean audio with modest gear and a treated space, and settle on a format and length you can maintain weekly.
levels.intermediate: Improve interviewing and editing, structure episodes for retention, and build distribution beyond hoping the platform surfaces you.
levels.advanced: Develop production values and narrative episodes, manage guests and a team, and handle sponsorship without losing the audience's trust.

name: Memory techniques
blurb: Making material stick — mnemonic structure for what you must recall, and scheduled retrieval for what you must retain.

levels.beginner: Learn the method of loci on something small, and understand why testing yourself beats rereading. Start a small deck with atomic cards rather than importing someone else's.
levels.intermediate: Apply memory systems to real material — vocabulary, anatomy, numbers — and combine them with review rather than treating them as a substitute for it.
levels.advanced: Build large reusable memory systems, tune scheduling and deck design for long-term collections, and recognise the material where neither mnemonics nor repetition substitutes for understanding.

name: Note-taking
blurb: Capturing information from lectures, meetings, and books in a form that's actually useful later.

levels.beginner: Stop transcribing. Learn a structured method and write in your own words, which is what makes notes worth having.
levels.intermediate: Match the method to the source — dense text, live lecture, meeting — and build a review habit so notes don't die in a folder.
levels.advanced: Develop note-taking that feeds directly into writing or decision-making, and cut the elaborate systems that produce more admin than insight.

name: Reading more and better
blurb: Reading consistently and retaining something from it, without turning it into a performance metric.

levels.beginner: Build the habit with books you actually want to read, and give yourself permission to abandon ones you don't.
levels.intermediate: Read actively — questions, marginalia, summaries — and vary approach between books you're studying and books you're enjoying.
levels.advanced: Read across a subject deliberately, engage critically with arguments and sources, and connect reading to writing or practice.

name: Language learning
blurb: Getting to genuine usability in another language through input, practice, and speaking earlier than feels comfortable.

levels.beginner: Build core vocabulary and basic grammar, get comprehensible input daily, and start speaking before you feel ready.
levels.intermediate: Push through the plateau with harder input, active output practice, and targeted work on the gaps you keep avoiding.
levels.advanced: Refine register, idiom, and listening in difficult conditions, and maintain multiple languages without losing the weaker ones.

name: Exam preparation
blurb: Preparing for high-stakes tests with methods that work, and managing the pressure around them.

levels.beginner: Replace rereading and highlighting with retrieval practice and past papers, and build a schedule that starts earlier than feels necessary.
levels.intermediate: Practise under exam conditions, diagnose errors by type, and allocate time to weaknesses rather than comfortable material.
levels.advanced: Prepare for professional or graduate-level exams with long timelines, and manage performance anxiety and pacing under real pressure.

name: Teaching yourself mathematics
blurb: Rebuilding mathematical ability from wherever your foundation broke, at your own pace.

levels.beginner: Find and fix the foundation gaps honestly, and do problems rather than watching explanations that feel clear until you try one.
levels.intermediate: Work through a structured curriculum with a real problem book, and learn to read mathematical writing slowly and actively.
levels.advanced: Engage with proof-based mathematics, build the habit of constructing arguments rather than applying procedures, and self-assess rigorously.

name: Research skills
blurb: Finding, assessing, and synthesising sources so your conclusions rest on something solid.

levels.beginner: Learn to search effectively, distinguish source types, and trace a claim back to its origin rather than to another summary.
levels.intermediate: Read papers efficiently, assess methodology and conflicts of interest, and organise sources so synthesis is possible.
levels.advanced: Conduct systematic reviews of a literature, weigh conflicting evidence by quality, and recognise the limits of what's been studied.

name: Critical thinking
blurb: Evaluating claims and arguments carefully, including the ones you already agree with.

levels.beginner: Learn to identify a claim, its evidence, and its assumptions, and to ask what would change your mind.
levels.intermediate: Assess argument quality and evidence strength, notice motivated reasoning in yourself, and hold uncertainty rather than picking a side early.
levels.advanced: Reason well about genuinely contested questions, calibrate confidence against outcomes, and avoid the trap of scepticism aimed only outward.

name: Deliberate practice
blurb: Structuring practice so it targets weaknesses with feedback, instead of repeating what you can already do.

levels.beginner: Identify a specific weakness, design a drill that isolates it, and get feedback fast enough to correct within the session.
levels.intermediate: Build practice sessions with clear objectives, use recording or coaching for feedback, and track progress on the sub-skill rather than the whole.
levels.advanced: Design long-term practice programmes across plateaus, and understand what the research does and doesn't claim about expertise development.

name: Teaching and explaining
blurb: Explaining ideas so someone else genuinely understands, which also exposes what you don't.

levels.beginner: Learn to start from what the listener already knows, use concrete examples first, and check understanding instead of asking if it makes sense.
levels.intermediate: Sequence material well, anticipate common misconceptions, and design practice for the learner rather than just presenting content.
levels.advanced: Teach difficult material to mixed groups, design curricula and assessment, and adapt live when the room isn't following.

name: Academic writing
blurb: Writing essays, theses, and papers with a clear argument and defensible use of sources.

levels.beginner: Learn essay structure, how to state a thesis, and how to cite properly. Write badly first and fix it in revision rather than stalling.
levels.intermediate: Build arguments that engage counter-positions, integrate sources rather than stacking quotes, and edit for clarity at sentence level.
levels.advanced: Write for publication in a field's conventions, handle peer review, and manage long projects like a thesis without losing the thread.

name: Task management systems
blurb: Running a trusted system for commitments, and reviewing it often enough to keep trusting it.

levels.beginner: Get everything out of your head into one list, define next actions physically, and book a short recurring slot to clear inboxes and choose what must happen next.
levels.intermediate: Organise by project and context, use a review cadence that keeps the system trustworthy, and resist tool-hopping as procrastination.
levels.advanced: Run a system across work and personal domains at high volume, review at multiple horizons — weekly, quarterly, annual — and simplify ruthlessly when maintenance starts exceeding value.

name: Deep work and focus
blurb: Building the capacity for sustained concentration on demanding work, and putting it in the hours you can actually do it.

levels.beginner: Remove the obvious interrupters and practise short focused sessions. Block time for your hardest work before the day fills up, and notice when in the day you are actually sharp.
levels.intermediate: Design an environment and schedule that make focus the default, and handle the internal distractions that survive turning off notifications.
levels.advanced: Sustain demanding cognitive work over long periods, design a calendar around energy and collaboration patterns rather than around meetings, and plan load and recovery across months rather than days.

name: Personal knowledge management
blurb: Building a notes system that connects ideas and produces output, not an archive you never revisit.

levels.beginner: Pick one tool and capture notes in your own words with light structure. Don't build an elaborate system before you have content in it.
levels.intermediate: Develop linking and resurfacing habits, write summary notes that synthesise rather than collect, and connect the system to actual output.
levels.advanced: Run a large knowledge base that supports serious writing or research, and prune the parts that generate maintenance rather than insight.

name: Email and inbox systems
blurb: Processing email quickly and reliably so it stops being the thing that eats your day.

levels.beginner: Process in batches rather than continuously, and use a simple rule set: reply, defer to your task system, delegate, or archive.
levels.intermediate: Build filters and templates, write emails that reduce round trips, and set expectations about response time explicitly.
levels.advanced: Handle very high volume with delegation and automation, and address the organisational habits generating unnecessary email in the first place.

name: Workflow automation
blurb: Automating repetitive work with scripts or no-code tools, without creating fragile systems only you can fix.

levels.beginner: Identify a genuinely repetitive task, automate it simply, and check that the time saved exceeds the time spent building it.
levels.intermediate: Chain tools together with error handling and logging, and document what you built so it's maintainable when it breaks.
levels.advanced: Build automation across a team or business with monitoring and ownership, and know when a process should be eliminated rather than automated.

name: Goal setting
blurb: Setting goals specific enough to act on and reviewing them honestly rather than quietly abandoning them.

levels.beginner: Convert vague ambitions into specific outcomes with a defined next action, and set fewer goals than feels satisfying.
levels.intermediate: Distinguish outcome, performance, and process goals, tie goals to weekly action, and review and revise rather than restarting each January.
levels.advanced: Set goals under uncertainty where the right target changes, and understand where goal-setting research is weaker than it's presented.

name: Digital minimalism
blurb: Deciding deliberately what technology gets access to your attention, and removing the rest.

levels.beginner: Audit where your screen time actually goes, then remove or add friction to the two worst offenders rather than everything at once.
levels.intermediate: Rebuild default behaviours and replace the removed habits with something you actually want to do, since a vacuum refills fast.
levels.advanced: Design a long-term relationship with technology that supports your work and relationships, and evaluate attention-economy claims critically rather than moralistically.

name: Prioritisation
blurb: Deciding what not to do, and making that decision explicitly instead of by default.

levels.beginner: Separate urgent from important in practice, and pick a single most-important task each day before opening anything else.
levels.intermediate: Use explicit criteria for trade-offs, say no with a reason, and prioritise across projects rather than only within a day.
levels.advanced: Make portfolio-level decisions where good options must be killed, and hold priorities against organisational pressure to do everything.

name: Spreadsheet skills
blurb: Using spreadsheets properly — formulas, structure, and models that don't quietly break.

levels.beginner: Learn core formulas, lookups, and clean data layout — one fact per cell, no merged cells in data ranges.
levels.intermediate: Build pivot tables, conditional logic, and charts, and structure workbooks so inputs, calculations, and outputs are separate.
levels.advanced: Build auditable models with sensitivity analysis, use scripting or advanced functions, and know when the job needs a database instead.

name: Dating
blurb: Meeting people, going on dates that reveal compatibility, and handling rejection without it derailing you.

levels.beginner: Learn the practical basics of meeting people and asking clearly, and treat early rejection as sorting rather than judgement.
levels.intermediate: Work out what you're actually looking for, communicate intentions honestly, and notice patterns in who you choose and why.
levels.advanced: Date with clarity about compatibility and values, handle the harder conversations early, and manage dating alongside a full life.

name: Long-term partnership
blurb: Keeping a long relationship healthy through repair, shared direction, and ordinary daily attention.

levels.beginner: Learn what actually predicts stability — repair after conflict, responsiveness to bids for attention — rather than absence of disagreement.
levels.intermediate: Handle recurring conflicts that won't resolve, negotiate labour and money explicitly, and maintain individual lives inside the relationship.
levels.advanced: Navigate major transitions — children, illness, career shifts — and rebuild connection after long periods of drift.

name: Couples communication
blurb: Talking about hard things with a partner in a way that ends better than it started.

levels.beginner: Learn soft start-ups, taking breaks when flooded, and stating a need rather than a criticism.
levels.intermediate: Work with recurring conflict cycles, understand each other's underlying concerns, and repair effectively after a bad exchange.
levels.advanced: Handle deep differences in values or life direction, and recognise when the pattern needs a therapist rather than better technique.

name: Parenting young children
blurb: Raising toddlers and young kids with realistic expectations of their development and your patience.

levels.beginner: Learn what's developmentally normal so behaviour stops reading as defiance, and get sleep and routine basics workable.
levels.intermediate: Handle limits and consequences consistently, support emotional development, and manage your own regulation when they're dysregulated.
levels.advanced: Address persistent difficulties, navigate schooling and screen decisions with evidence, and adapt when a child's needs differ from the standard advice.

name: Parenting teenagers
blurb: Staying connected to an adolescent while the relationship's terms change under you.

levels.beginner: Understand adolescent development, and shift from directing to negotiating while keeping a small number of non-negotiables.
levels.intermediate: Keep communication open about risk topics without lecturing, handle autonomy and monitoring, and repair after conflict.
levels.advanced: Support a teenager through mental health difficulties or serious risk, and manage the transition to an adult-to-adult relationship.

name: Making friends as an adult
blurb: Building real friendships after school, when nothing puts you in the same room repeatedly by default.

levels.beginner: Prioritise repeated contact over perfect chemistry: join something recurring, and be the person who suggests the next meeting.
levels.intermediate: Move acquaintances toward friendship through initiation and appropriate vulnerability, and maintain contact without it feeling like admin.
levels.advanced: Build a durable network through life changes and relocation, and repair or let go of friendships that have quietly ended.

name: Setting boundaries
blurb: Saying what you will and won't do, clearly and without a long justification, then holding it.

levels.beginner: Learn that a boundary is about your own action, not controlling theirs, and practise declining small things without over-explaining.
levels.intermediate: Hold boundaries under pushback and guilt, and distinguish a boundary from an ultimatum or a punishment.
levels.advanced: Set boundaries in relationships with real power or dependency involved, and handle the consequences when someone won't accept them.

name: Attachment patterns
blurb: Understanding how early relational patterns shape adult closeness, without using the labels as a personality test.

levels.beginner: Learn what the attachment categories describe and what they don't, and notice your own patterns under stress rather than in the abstract.
levels.intermediate: Work with the specific behaviours — protest, withdrawal, testing — and how partners' patterns interact and escalate each other.
levels.advanced: Engage with the research honestly, including its limits and how much attachment shifts with relationship and time rather than being fixed.

name: Breakups and divorce
blurb: Ending a relationship and rebuilding afterwards, including the practical parts nobody prepares you for.

levels.beginner: Get through the acute phase: routine, support, and no contact where that's appropriate, plus the immediate practical decisions.
levels.intermediate: Process what happened without either self-blame or full blame, handle shared logistics and children, and rebuild a separate life.
levels.advanced: Address long-term patterns that contributed, co-parent civilly over years, and re-enter relationships without carrying the same expectations.

name: Caring for ageing parents
blurb: Supporting parents through decline — the logistics, the family negotiations, and your own limits.

levels.beginner: Have the early conversations about wishes, finances, and documents before a crisis forces them, and map what support exists.
levels.intermediate: Coordinate care and medical decisions, negotiate responsibility among siblings, and protect your own health and work.
levels.advanced: Handle dementia care, end-of-life decisions, and the grief that starts long before the death itself.

name: Intimacy and sexual health
blurb: Talking about sex with a partner and getting accurate information rather than folklore.

levels.beginner: Get factual basics on anatomy, consent, and contraception, and learn to raise the subject with a partner without it being a confrontation.
levels.intermediate: Handle mismatched desire, understand how stress, health, and medication affect it, and communicate preferences specifically.
levels.advanced: Address persistent difficulties with proper clinical or therapeutic support, and navigate long-term changes with age and health.

name: Rebuilding trust
blurb: Repairing a relationship after a betrayal or a long erosion, or deciding honestly that you won't.

levels.beginner: Understand what repair actually requires from both sides, and that the decision to try does not have to be made immediately.
levels.intermediate: Work through disclosure, accountability, and the long period of inconsistent progress that follows, usually with professional help.
levels.advanced: Rebuild a genuinely different relationship rather than restoring the old one, or separate with clarity when repair isn't happening.

name: Home cooking fundamentals
blurb: Cooking without a recipe by understanding heat, seasoning, and technique rather than memorising dishes.

levels.beginner: Learn knife handling, heat control, and seasoning by cooking the same few dishes repeatedly until you stop needing the recipe.
levels.intermediate: Understand technique families — braising, roasting, emulsions, pan sauces — and start improvising from what's in the fridge.
levels.advanced: Develop palate and timing to cook several components to land together, and adapt technique across cuisines with an understanding of why it works.

name: Baking
blurb: Baking bread and pastry with an understanding of ratios, gluten, and fermentation rather than blind recipe-following.

levels.beginner: Learn to measure by weight and follow one recipe until it's reliable, understanding what each ingredient does before substituting.
levels.intermediate: Work with hydration, fermentation, and lamination, and diagnose failures from the dough's behaviour rather than guessing.
levels.advanced: Develop and scale your own formulas, control fermentation across conditions, and handle advanced pastry with consistency.

name: Car maintenance
blurb: Doing basic servicing yourself and knowing enough to have an informed conversation with a mechanic.

levels.beginner: Learn fluids, tyres, brakes, and warning lights, and do the simple jobs safely with proper support and torque.
levels.intermediate: Diagnose common faults, read fault codes, and take on brake, suspension, and servicing work with the right tools.
levels.advanced: Handle engine, transmission, or electrical work, and judge when a repair is beyond a home setup or economically pointless.

name: Home repair and DIY
blurb: Fixing and improving your home safely, and recognising the jobs that legally or sensibly need a professional.

levels.beginner: Build a basic tool kit and learn wall fixings, filling, painting, and simple plumbing, plus how to isolate water and power safely.
levels.intermediate: Handle tiling, flooring, carpentry, and straightforward plumbing, and plan projects with sequencing and materials in mind.
levels.advanced: Manage larger renovations, understand structural and regulatory limits, and coordinate trades where the work isn't yours to do.

name: Gardening
blurb: Growing plants successfully by working with your soil, climate, and light rather than against them.

levels.beginner: Learn your light, soil, and climate, then grow a few forgiving plants well rather than many badly.
levels.intermediate: Work on soil health, propagation, and succession planting, and manage pests and disease with proportionate responses.
levels.advanced: Design planting for year-round productivity or ecological function, save seed, and adapt to changing conditions over seasons.

name: First aid
blurb: Knowing what to do in the first minutes of an emergency, from bleeding control to CPR.

levels.beginner: Learn to assess a scene, call for help correctly, control severe bleeding, and perform CPR with an AED. Hands-on certification beats video alone.
levels.intermediate: Handle a wider range of emergencies — burns, fractures, allergic reaction, choking — and maintain a genuinely useful kit.
levels.advanced: Manage prolonged care where help is delayed, such as remote or wilderness settings, and keep certification current with practice.

name: Sewing and mending
blurb: Repairing and altering clothes so they last, and making garments that actually fit.

levels.beginner: Learn hand stitches and basic machine use, and start with repairs — buttons, hems, seams — on clothes you already own.
levels.intermediate: Work from patterns, adjust for fit, and handle different fabrics with the right needle, tension, and finishing.
levels.advanced: Draft or heavily modify patterns, tailor structured garments, and achieve finishing that stands up to close inspection.

name: Decluttering and organising
blurb: Reducing what you own and building systems so your space stays workable without constant tidying.

levels.beginner: Start with an easy category and decide by what you actually use, then deal with what leaves rather than moving it to another room.
levels.intermediate: Build systems where things have obvious homes, address the inflow that recreates clutter, and handle sentimental items honestly.
levels.advanced: Manage shared spaces where others don't share your standards, and handle large clearances such as a family home or an inherited estate.

name: Travel planning
blurb: Planning trips that work — routing, budgeting, and booking — without overplanning them into a schedule.

levels.beginner: Learn how to research a destination properly, budget realistically including the costs people forget, and pack light.
levels.intermediate: Work flight and accommodation pricing, build flexible itineraries, and handle visas, insurance, and health requirements.
levels.advanced: Plan complex multi-country or long-term travel, manage risk and logistics in difficult regions, and travel with less impact on the places you visit.

name: Bike maintenance
blurb: Keeping a bicycle running well — the routine jobs that prevent most roadside failures.

levels.beginner: Learn punctures, chain cleaning, and brake and gear adjustment, and get the few tools that make these jobs quick.
levels.intermediate: Handle bearing servicing, cable and hydraulic brake work, and wear diagnosis before parts fail on a ride.
levels.advanced: Build wheels, service suspension, and set up a bike precisely for fit and conditions.

name: Coffee brewing
blurb: Brewing consistently good coffee by controlling grind, ratio, and extraction rather than buying more equipment.

levels.beginner: Learn ratio, grind size, and fresh beans. A decent grinder changes more than an expensive brewer.
levels.intermediate: Dial in by taste using extraction principles, learn several brew methods, and keep equipment clean enough not to taint the cup.
levels.advanced: Work with espresso variables and profiling, evaluate coffee critically by origin and roast, and troubleshoot systematically rather than by feel.

name: Camping and outdoor skills
blurb: Being comfortable and safe outdoors — navigation, shelter, and judgement about conditions.

levels.beginner: Learn layering, shelter, and food and water basics, and plan a first trip within your fitness and daylight rather than your ambition.
levels.intermediate: Navigate with map and compass rather than only GPS, manage weather and terrain judgement, and lighten your load sensibly.
levels.advanced: Handle multi-day remote trips, winter or alpine conditions, and the risk assessment and self-rescue skills those require.

name: Personal style and grooming
blurb: Dressing and presenting yourself deliberately — fit, proportion, and a wardrobe that suits your actual life rather than trends.

levels.beginner: Learn fit before anything else — it matters more than brand, price or trend. Work out what you actually wear in a normal week before buying anything.
levels.intermediate: Build a coherent wardrobe around your real life and climate, understand proportion and colour on your own body, and learn basic alteration and care.
levels.advanced: Develop a personal register that reads consistently across contexts, judge quality and construction directly, and stop needing external rules for it.

name: Stoicism
blurb: Reading the Stoics seriously as philosophy, not as a productivity brand for enduring a bad job.

levels.beginner: Read a primary text rather than a summary, and learn the core distinction between what is and isn't within your control.
levels.intermediate: Understand Stoic ethics, physics, and logic as a connected system, and where the popular version drops most of it.
levels.advanced: Engage with scholarship and the serious objections, and compare Stoic positions with rival ancient and modern ethical accounts.

name: Existentialism
blurb: Working through freedom, responsibility, and absurdity with the thinkers who took them seriously.

levels.beginner: Start with the accessible primary works and grasp the central claims about freedom, anxiety, and self-deception.
levels.intermediate: Read the major figures against each other, and follow the argument from phenomenology into existentialist ethics and politics.
levels.advanced: Engage with the dense primary texts and the secondary literature, and situate existentialism against its critics and successors.

name: Ethics
blurb: Reasoning about right action with the major frameworks, and applying them to cases that resist easy answers.

levels.beginner: Learn the main normative frameworks and what each gets right and wrong, and practise applying them to concrete cases.
levels.intermediate: Engage with metaethics — what moral claims even are — and with applied debates where the frameworks genuinely diverge.
levels.advanced: Work through the contemporary literature on specific problems, and hold a considered position you can defend against strong objections.

name: Eastern philosophy
blurb: Studying Buddhist, Daoist, and other traditions as rigorous philosophy rather than as wellness content.

levels.beginner: Get an accurate overview of the major traditions and their central claims, distinguishing them from the Western wellness repackaging.
levels.intermediate: Read primary texts in good translation with commentary, and understand the internal debates within each tradition.
levels.advanced: Engage with the scholarly literature and comparative philosophy, and take the metaphysical and epistemological arguments on their own terms.

name: Philosophy of mind
blurb: Thinking rigorously about consciousness, perception, and what a mind actually is.

levels.beginner: Learn the main positions on the mind-body problem and why the hard problem of consciousness is framed as hard.
levels.intermediate: Work through arguments about intentionality, personal identity, and free will, and engage with the empirical findings that bear on them.
levels.advanced: Read the contemporary literature closely, including work at the boundary with neuroscience and artificial intelligence.

name: Meaning and purpose
blurb: Thinking carefully about what makes a life worth living, beyond finding your passion.

levels.beginner: Separate meaning from happiness and from career, and examine which of your current commitments you'd actually endorse on reflection.
levels.intermediate: Engage with the philosophical accounts of meaning and with the empirical work on wellbeing, noting where they disagree.
levels.advanced: Work through the harder positions — nihilism, absurdism, objective versus subjective accounts — and hold a view you can live with.

name: Mortality and death
blurb: Thinking and talking about death honestly, philosophically and practically, before it's urgent.

levels.beginner: Learn to think about mortality without either denial or morbidity, and handle the practical side: wills, wishes, and conversations.
levels.intermediate: Engage with the philosophical arguments about whether death is bad, and with what palliative and hospice care actually involve.
levels.advanced: Work through the harder debates — assisted dying, medical decision-making at the end of life — and support others facing them.
